title: Complete sync change pages v1
description: A bounded complete stream page. Reading does not acknowledge, apply payloads or prove local persistence. Legacy event payloads and extra historical fields remain reference data.
$comment: Source-only companion to sync-changes.ts. Register this and sync-consumer.json under full IDs. Runtime enforces 4 KiB decoded query, 16 KiB local request with optional identity and 4 MiB complete envelope, ordinary finite JSON/depth64/100000 nodes, UTF-16/Unicode limits, exact scope/trace, ordered unique event positions and exact flattened sources. No full business-event validation or authentication is implied by this schema.

SyncChangesQuery.description: Decoded HTTP numeric query. Omitted cursor resumes from the authenticated consumer's current acknowledgement, or zero if absent; explicit cursor=0 reads from zero. Omission must not be normalized to a schema default of zero.

SyncChangesRequest.description: Local SDK/MCP request including optional saved consumer identity. HTTP only sends cursor/limit in URL; identity maps to scope and actor/client precondition headers, never an expected_identity query string.

sourceRef.$comment: Matches validateSourceRef: known strings are nonempty, not required to be trimmed or valid URIs; optional revision is a nonnegative safe integer. Historical extra source fields are preserved and participate in outer-source equality, so do not replace this with the closed item-history SourceRef.

SyncChange.$comment: When present, event scope fields equal the page scope. Event IDs are unique within the page; cursors strictly ascend beyond an explicit input cursor (shared parser uses zero when omitted) and never exceed next_cursor. Saved trace may differ from request trace. This intentionally is not a full CanonicalEvent union: Gateway expands valid canonical stored records, but wraps noncanonical legacy records as payload and preserves extras. accepted=true is stream acceptance, not successful client application or approval.

SyncChangesEnvelope.$comment: Outer server_cursor=data.next_cursor>=explicit input cursor, count<=requested/default limit. With has_more=true, count equals limit and next_cursor is the last event cursor; otherwise Gateway uses the transaction's high-water mark, even on an empty filtered page. Outer sources exactly concatenate each event's source_refs in event order, retaining duplicates and extra fields; JSON object-key ordering is irrelevant. Each page has its own database snapshot. No identity echo beyond scope, ETag, revision, automatic acknowledgement or complete-history promise.
